title: Glienicke Bridge - FAQ
subtitle: Getting there, the spy exchanges, tickets and what is open.

items.q: Why is Glienicke Bridge called the Bridge of Spies?
items.a: Because East and West used it **three times** to exchange agents and prisoners: on **10 February 1962** (Rudolf Abel for Francis Gary Powers), on **11 June 1985** (23 people for four Eastern agents) and on **11 February 1986** (Anatoly Shcharansky and three others for five).

items.q: How do I get to Glienicke Bridge from central Berlin?
items.a: Take the **S7 to Wannsee**, about 32 minutes from Alexanderplatz, then **bus 316** to Glienicker Brücke, about 13 minutes. From Potsdam Hauptbahnhof, **tram 93** takes about 13 minutes.

items.q: Is an AB ticket enough for Glienicke Bridge?
items.a: Not for the last stop. The **Glienicker Brücke stop is in fare zone C**. With an AB ticket, get off at **Schloss Glienicke**, the stop before, and walk the last few minutes onto the bridge. Buy **ABC** if you want to continue into Potsdam.

items.q: Can you walk across Glienicke Bridge?
items.a: Yes. It is an ordinary road bridge with pavements, open to everyone since the evening of **10 November 1989**. A **metal strip** in the middle of the deck marks where the border ran.

items.q: Was Bridge of Spies filmed on the real bridge?
items.a: Yes. Steven Spielberg filmed on Glienicke Bridge in **late 2014**, with the bridge closed for about a week. The film came out in 2015.

A small part of the Wannsee district that lay **entirely inside GDR territory**, cut off from the rest of West Berlin. After 1961 US helicopters supplied it. A road corridor opened on **30 August 1972**. A memorial with two rotor blades stands on the old landing pad at Am Landeplatz.

items.q: Is Villa Schöningen open in winter?
items.a: In winter it opens **Friday to Sunday, 11:00 to 17:00**. A ticket costs **EUR 8**, EUR 5 reduced and free under 18. Check the current exhibition before you go.

items.q: How long do I need for Glienicke Bridge?
items.a: The bridge alone takes about **an hour** from Wannsee and back. With Steinstücken, the park at Schloss Glienicke and Villa Schöningen, plan **about three hours** on the ground, plus the S-Bahn from the centre.
